turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt his way down the dark hallway, his heart heavy with a mix of fear and wonder as he searched for Estella, the girl Miss Havisham had asked for.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham waited silently, her eyes narrowing as she heard Pip's footsteps fade down the hallway. She knew the boy was curious, perhaps even fearful, but she also sensed a spark of something else, something she might mold.

turns.text: Miss Havisham watched the boy's retreating figure with a mixture of disdain and intrigue, her thoughts swirling with the potential this visit held.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip returned to the parlor, his footsteps echoing softly on the stone floor, his heart still racing with a mix of fear and curiosity.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: She watched as Pip returned to the parlor, his presence stirring a mix of emotions within her. A spark of interest flickered in her eyes, though her expression remained cold and distant.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip looked nervously around the parlor, his eyes darting from the decayed wedding cake to the rusted clocks, each one frozen at the same hour.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: She observed the boy's unease, his eyes wide with the strange sights of her decaying world, and her heart stirred with a twisted sense of pleasure.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt Miss Havisham's eyes on him, making him feel small and uncomfortable, yet there was something compelling about her that drew him closer, if only to better understand the strange woman.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: She fixed her gaze on the boy, a mixture of disdain and fascination in her eyes, and spoke in a commanding tone, as if commanding the boy to look beyond the decay and see the deeper truths.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt the weight of Miss Havisham’s gaze and hesitantly met her eyes, trying to understand the emotions playing across her face.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt compelled to look around despite his discomfort, as if he were trying to solve a puzzle that Miss Havisham had set for him.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham gestured for Pip to approach, her voice dripping with an enigmatic command, as if she could peel away the layers of his youth to see the man within.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt the weight of Miss Havisham’s command and, though uneasy, stepped closer to her, as if he were being drawn by some strange curiosity.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: She peered into Pip's eyes, her own clouded with a mix of bitterness and longing, as if searching for something within him that mirrored her own fractured soul.

turns.speaker: Pip

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Pip, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Pip?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip informed Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer; let her look at him. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was not afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched here?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he did, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip what she touched?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that it was broken!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired. She wanted diversion, and she had done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies, and she had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was not, ma’am, he was very sorry for her, and very sorry he could not play just now. If she complained of him he would get into trouble with his sister, so he would do it if he could; but it was so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham remarked that it was so new to him, so old to her; so strange to him, so familiar to her; so melancholy to both of them! She asked Pip to call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to call Estella. At the door.
